bass2_flame_spread.step: load NASA PSI-25 / Link et al. 2018 Table S1
bass2_flame_spread.why: verified extract of measured spread rates

bass2_flame_spread.step: keep flow steps as separate rows, group = ISS test
bass2_flame_spread.why: flow changes within a test; rows of one test share hardware and are not independent

bass2_flame_spread.step: physics space: log O2, log(1/diameter), log flow + flow; target log(spread)
bass2_flame_spread.why: spread follows power laws in O2 and rod size (thin-rod spread ~ 1/d); in microgravity spread first rises with opposed flow (more O2 delivered) then falls (flame cooled/blown off), so flow enters as u^a * exp(b*u)

bass2_flame_spread.step: noise prior from 39 near-replicate pairs (log scale)
bass2_flame_spread.why: the GP starts from measured run-to-run noise instead of guessing it

flex_extinction.step: drop 68 tests: 61 'Disruption' (no clean outcome) + 7 with droplet size or pressure missing in the NASA file
flex_extinction.why: a droplet that broke up has neither extinguished nor burned out: its label is undefined

flex_extinction.step: physics features: O2 partial pressure, log pressure, diluent %, droplet size, fuel
flex_extinction.why: extinction depends on how much O2 reaches the flame (partial pressure), heat loss (size, diluent) and fuel

flex_extinction.step: group = FLEX test series (first 3 characters of the FLEX id)
flex_extinction.why: a series shares the same chamber fill; whole series are held out

flex_burning_rate.step: drop 16 tests without K, 1 with K <= 0.1 and those missing size or pressure
flex_burning_rate.why: K is the slope of the d^2-law; it must be measured and physical

flex_burning_rate.step: physics features (same as extinction); target K in mm^2/s
flex_burning_rate.why: d^2-law: K = (8k / rho c_p) ln(1+B); B grows with available O2, falls with diluent
measured run-to-run noise for the GP

spice_smoke_point.why: the sheet that holds measured smoke points (not test settings)

spice_smoke_point.step: physics space: log burner diameter, log coflow, fuel; target log(smoke-point length)
spice_smoke_point.why: smoke-point length follows a power law in burner size and coflow (Dotson et al. 2011)
a session shares hardware state and calibration

spice_smoke_point.step: noise prior from 16 near-replicate pairs (log scale)
spice_smoke_point.why: measured run-to-run noise for the GP

same_particle_size.step: drop 24 readings with all particle moments = 0 or '#NUM!'
same_particle_size.why: an instrument/reduction failure, not a real zero-size smoke

same_particle_size.step: drop readings with '??' temperature or missing aging time
same_particle_size.why: the input is unknown, so the row cannot teach the model

same_particle_size.step: features: temperature, airflow, log aging time, material, campaign; target log(diameter)
same_particle_size.why: particle size spans a factor ~20, so errors are relative; aging coagulates particles roughly logarithmically in time

same_particle_size.step: group = run (fresh + aged reading of the same run kept together)
same_particle_size.why: the aged reading is the same smoke measured later

same_particle_size.step: noise prior from 164 near-replicate pairs (log scale)
same_particle_size.why: measured run-to-run noise for the GP
